newsitem.title: UK: London gold fixing slumps to 2-1/2 year low.
newsitem.headline: London gold fixing slumps to 2-1/2 year low.

text.p: The gold market weakened to its lowest fixing in over 2-1/2 years on Thursday as investors continued their retreat from the yellow metal.
Bullion was fixed at $372.20 per ounce in London, down from $373.00 on Wednesday marking its lowest setting since April 25, 1994.
Dealers said soaring stock markets and a stronger dollar were pulling investor money out of gold.
"A hefty fall in the Dow or the dollar coming off will be needed to get some interest in gold again," one dealer said.
The market has been unnerved recently by concerns that European central banks might be tempted to sell gold in the run-up to European Monetary Union.
Other concerns have centred on the International Monetary Fund selling part of its gold reserves and the possibility of increased exports being permitted by the Russian government.
